entry.title: The Evolution of the SAP User Interface: From SAP GUI to Fiori to Joule Work
entry.content:
The Evolution of the SAP User Interface: From SAP GUI to Fiori to Joule Work

From transactions to intuitive apps to AI-powered collaboration – the SAP user experience is not just changing its appearance. It is changing the way we work.

Anyone who has worked with SAP for a long time will remember it: the classic SAP GUI, countless transaction codes, complex screens, and a user interface that was primarily designed to do one thing – provide functionality.

But the world has changed. And so have our expectations of enterprise software.

Looking back, we can see just how far we have come – and what this evolution means for us as people.

1. SAP GUI – The Era of Transactions

Throughout the 1990s and well beyond, SAP GUI was the central entry point to business processes in countless companies.

The interface was powerful, stable, and designed to support complex business processes. To use SAP efficiently, users had to become familiar with transaction codes, screens, fields, and process logic.

People had to learn how SAP worked.

Over the years, experienced users developed an enormous amount of knowledge. They knew which transaction to use, which fields mattered, and which steps were required to achieve the desired result.

It worked – but shift began in the design of the user experience.

Instead of complex transaction screens, the focus moved towards role-based apps, modern design, and more intuitive interaction. The user experience became increasingly aligned with people's tasks and needs.

Information was meant to be easier to access. Processes were meant to become more understandable. And SAP was increasingly expected to feel as intuitive as the modern applications we use in everyday life.

The key question changed: Not just “How does this transaction work?” but “What task do I want to accomplish?”

With Fiori, access to SAP became more modern, flexible, and better suited to different roles and devices.

This was more than a new design. It was an important step towards a better user experience and a stronger focus on people.

3. Joule Work – From Using Software to AI-Powered Collaboration

With generative AI, the next chapter of the SAP user experience is beginning.

AI assistants such as Joule make it possible to ask for information in natural language, understand relationships more quickly, and receive intelligent support when completing certain tasks.

With Joule Work, SAP is taking this approach further towards an AI-powered work environment. The aim is to bring information and work contexts together more effectively and support tasks across different applications and business processes.

Instead of navigating exclusively through menus and applications, users can increasingly describe what they want to achieve.

Imagine a typical business scenario:

Instead of opening multiple reports and manually compiling data, a user could ask:

“Analyze sales performance over the past three months, identify the largest deviations, and summarize the most important areas for action.”

The vision is for AI to help users find information, analyze data, and prepare decisions – and, depending on available capabilities and permissions, also assist in executing tasks.

People will spend less time searching for information and more time interpreting it and making the right decisions.

An important point: Not every task can already be fully automated. The actual benefits depend on the available capabilities, integration with business processes, and the quality of the underlying data.

4. The Real Change Is About People

The evolution of the SAP user interface is therefore not just a story about technology.

It is also a story about how our work is changing.

Era What matters most What it means for people

SAP GUITransactions and screensSystem knowledge and process expertise are essential
SAP FioriApps and tasksMore intuitive interaction and easier access to information
Joule Work and AIIntent, context, and assistanceGreater focus on analysis, decisions, and collaboration

This evolution raises important questions.

Which skills will become more important in the future?

Knowledge of individual transactions will remain valuable in many areas. At the same time, other skills will become increasingly important: asking the right questions, critically evaluating results, understanding business processes, and using AI effectively.

The roles of IT departments, SAP consultants, and process owners are also changing. It is no longer just about configuring systems correctly and training users. Increasingly, it is about designing intelligent workflows, making meaningful use of data, and helping people adapt to a new world of work.

And this is where a major challenge lies: New technology alone does not change the way people work. Real value is created only when people understand, trust, and use it effectively.

5. What Does This Mean for SAP Transformations?

For companies, one important insight emerges: The evolution of the user interface should not be treated as an isolated IT project.

Organizations modernizing SAP should also rethink their workflows, employee roles, data quality, and opportunities for automation.

Some key questions to consider:

  • Which tasks can be simplified through better user experience and guidance?

  • Where can AI assistants make information available more quickly?

  • Which processes are suitable for further automation?

  • How can we ensure that employees understand and embrace the new possibilities?

  • How do we measure whether productivity, quality, and employee satisfaction are actually improving?

Especially in the SAP ecosystem, it will be crucial to develop technology, processes, and people together.

Because a modern interface is not an end in itself. It must make work easier, better, and more meaningful.

Conclusion: Less Time Operating Systems. More Time Making an Impact.

From SAP GUI through SAP Fiori to Joule Work, we are witnessing an evolution that goes far beyond the design of a user interface.

We are moving from a world where people had to learn how to operate the system, through a world of intuitive, task-oriented applications, towards a way of working in which AI increasingly understands, assists, and supports tasks.

The exciting question is therefore no longer just what the next SAP interface will look like.

The real question is: How much more can people achieve when technology takes some of the complexity off their shoulders?

The future of SAP will not be measured solely by how intelligent the systems become. It will be measured by how effectively they help people make better decisions, collaborate more efficiently, and focus on what truly matters.

Less complexity. More intelligence. More time for what really matters.
